targetAudience: PMs and leaders pitching AI investments
topic: A one-page AI business case that finance will accept
coreInsight: A fundable AI business case fits on one page with five boxes — baseline, the one number AI should move, cost at full volume, what happens when it’s wrong, and a decision date — and without a baseline you’re not ready to ask.

Why your AI pitch keeps getting “not yet”.

caption:
A great demo answers “can it work?” Finance is asking “what changes, at what cost, and when do we know?”

Five boxes on one page:
→ Baseline: how the task performs today, measured
→ Change: the one number AI should move
→ Cost envelope: run cost at full volume, not PoC volume
→ Risk: what happens when it’s wrong, and who catches it
→ Decision date: when you stop or scale

Start with the baseline. If nobody has measured the task today, measure that first.

(The invoice-triage numbers in the reel are an illustrative example.)

Save this before you pitch finance.

claims.text: An AI business case is more likely to be funded when it states a measured baseline, one target metric, full-volume run cost, failure handling and a decision date.
Invoice triage at 6 minutes per invoice today with a target under 2 minutes and a day-60 decision.
